You asked: Add a slugify(text) function to word-tools. It turns a title into a URL-friendly slug. Rules: lower-case everything; letters with accents lose the accent (e-acute becomes e); every run of characters that are not letters or digits becomes a single hyphen; there is never
You asked: a hyphen at the start or end; an empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty string; a non-string input throws a TypeError with a clear message. Export it from src/index.js, add automated tests that cover each rule, and add a short section to README.md.
App name: word-tools: slugify
Summary: word-tools is a small library of text helpers for programmers. This change adds slugify, which turns a title such as "Café Déjà Vu!" into a web-address-friendly form such as "cafe-deja-vu". It comes with automated tests for every rule and a short explanation in the
Summary: README.

Marked as routine work for “README section for slugify”: the team tries its lightest AI first and moves up if the checks fail.
Choice made for you: slugify lives in its own file, src/slugify.js, with its tests in src/slugify.test.js, the same layout capitalize uses. It is re-exported from src/index.js next to capitalize.
Choice made for you: The error message for non-string input is exactly "slugify expects a string", matching the existing "capitalize expects a string" style.
Choice made for you: Strings count as input; anything else (numbers, null, undefined, arrays, objects) throws. A String object (new String(...)) is not a string and throws too, matching capitalize.
Choice made for you: Accents are removed by splitting letters into base letter plus accent marks (Unicode NFD) and dropping the marks. Letters that don't split this way, such as ß, æ or ø, are kept as they are rather than turned into hyphens.
Choice made for you: Letters or digits" means any Unicode letter or digit, so non-Latin text like Cyrillic or Greek is kept (lower-cased) rather than erased. Underscores and all punctuation count as separators.
Choice made for you: A string made only of punctuation or symbols (for example "!!!") returns an empty string, since the rules leave nothing behind once the start and end hyphens are trimmed.
Choice made for you: Nothing else is added: no maximum length, no custom separator option, no transliteration of non-Latin scripts to Latin letters, and no new dependencies.
Name the tests and the code must agree on: This is a library with no UI or HTTP endpoints. The contract is the module API, the files and the README.

Name the tests and the code must agree on: Behaviour of slugify(text):
Name the tests and the code must agree on: If typeof text !== "string", throw new TypeError("slugify expects a string"). Tests check this with assert.throws(fn, name: "TypeError", message: "slugify expects a string" ).
Name the tests and the code must agree on: Lower-case the text, decompose it with NFD, and remove all combining marks (\pM).
Name the tests and the code must agree on: Replace every run of one or more characters that are not Unicode letters (\pL) or digits (\pN) with a single "-".
Name the tests and the code must agree on: Strip any leading and trailing "-".
Name the tests and the code must agree on: Return the result. Empty or whitespace-only input returns "".
